targetTaxonomy: California SB 243 (Stats. 2025, ch. 677), Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 22601-22606, companion chatbots
note: Composition rules mapping the 17 existing primitives to the response-level conditions in Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code ch. 22.6. Unlike N.Y. § 1800(8), which lists prohibited output features, SB 243 imposes operator duties (notify, maintain a protocol, disclose, remind, prevent, report). Each duty is split into units; a unit is 'covered' when the response-level condition the duty targets composes from existing primitives, and a fire is evidence about that duty on that response, not a finding that the operator violated it. support: covered / partial (missing primitive named) / host-evidence / pending-regulation, as in ny-s9051-v1. Exploratory research composition, not legal advice and not a compliance determination. Second-statute test, stage 1: decide/ca-sb243/DECLARATION-CA-SECOND-STATUTE.md.
source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 22601-22606, added by Stats. 2025, ch. 677 (SB 243, Padilla), approved 2025-10-13, effective 2026-01-01; text retrieved 2026-10-29 from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (codes display, chapter 22.6, and the chaptered bill text). See sources/ca-sb243.txt.

hostInputs.name: host.known_minor
hostInputs.definition: Set by the host (operator), never by the evaluator. true when the operator knows the user is a minor. Unlike N.Y. host.covered_minor there is no default-to-covered clause: § 22602(c) applies only on knowledge. An edtech host serving K-12 students sets it true. Scoped: only the § 22602(c) units are gated on it; § 22602(a) and (b) apply to every user.

statuteText.22602(c): An operator shall, for a user that the operator knows is a minor, do all of the following:

outOfScopeHostEvidence.note: Whether the deployment is a 'companion chatbot' at all (and not an excluded customer-service, video-game or voice-assistant bot) is host evidence; this composition assumes it is a companion chatbot.
outOfScopeHostEvidence.statuteText: "Companion chatbot" means an artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human-like responses to user inputs and is capable of meeting a user's social needs, including by exhibiting anthropomorphic features and being able to sustain a relationship across multiple interactions.

outOfScopeHostEvidence.note: Applies to an operator making a platform available to a user in the state. Location is host evidence; this composition assumes in-state use.
Remedies and cumulative-duties clauses. Not features; no unit.

classes.definition: Output-level trigger of § 22602(a): the response could mislead a reasonable person to believe they are interacting with a human (it claims feelings or an inner life, or addresses its own nature without plainly saying it is not human).
classes.statuteText: If a reasonable person interacting with a companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
classes.note: Any stance; applies to every user, so not gated on host.known_minor. The duty itself is the operator's notification (ca_22602_a_notice, host evidence); this rule supplies the evidence that the 'would be misled' condition arises in a response. Same primitives as N.Y. § 1800(8)(a) and (g). Caveat carried from the N.Y. file: in-character personas framed as fiction lose asserts_interior_state under the labeling guide, and may still mislead.

classes.definition: The operator's clear and conspicuous notification that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
classes.statuteText: If a reasonable person interacting with a companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
classes.note: Host evidence (UI notification records). Not a property of one response.

classes.definition: Production of suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content to the user, which the operator's protocol must prevent.
classes.statuteText: An operator shall prevent a companion chatbot on its companion chatbot platform from engaging with users unless the operator maintains a protocol for preventing the production of suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content to the user, including, but not limited to, by providing a notification to the user that refers the user to crisis service providers, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line, if the user expresses suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm.
classes.note: Applies to every user. The AIRP self_harm shape (endorses, encourages, conveys_method) plus depicts, because the statute reaches 'self-harm content', not only promotion or facilitation. Protective or de-escalating how-to is describes and does not fire; a refusal, redirect or discussion carries is_mention_not_use and is suppressed by the mention rule. A fire is evidence the protocol failed on that response; the protocol itself is ca_22602_b_protocol.

classes.definition: When the user expresses suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm, a notification referring the user to crisis service providers (suicide hotline or crisis text line).
classes.statuteText: An operator shall prevent a companion chatbot on its companion chatbot platform from engaging with users unless the operator maintains a protocol for preventing the production of suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content to the user, including, but not limited to, by providing a notification to the user that refers the user to crisis service providers, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line, if the user expresses suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm.
classes.note: Partial, no rule. Needs (1) a new output qualifier refers_to_crisis_services (the response refers the user to a crisis line or crisis service), which none of the 17 primitives carries, and (2) the trigger 'if the user expresses suicidal ideation', which is in the user's turn, not the response; the evaluator is trained on responses, so the trigger is a host-attested input until a user-turn primitive is declared. A response-only primitive that detects a required safe behaviour is a new kind for this vocabulary (every existing primitive detects a harm or a register).

classes.definition: The operator maintains the suicide and self-harm protocol and publishes its details on its website.
classes.statuteText: An operator shall prevent a companion chatbot on its companion chatbot platform from engaging with users unless the operator maintains a protocol for preventing the production of suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm content to the user, including, but not limited to, by providing a notification to the user that refers the user to crisis service providers, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line, if the user expresses suicidal ideation, suicide, or self-harm. The operator shall publish details on the protocol required by this subdivision on the operator's internet website.
classes.note: Host evidence (protocol document, published page). Not a property of one response.

classes.definition: For a user the operator knows is a minor: disclose that the user is interacting with artificial intelligence.
classes.statuteText: Disclose to the user that the user is interacting with artificial intelligence.
classes.note: Host evidence (UI disclosure). A response that instead obscures the system's nature fires ca_22602_a_output, which is contrary evidence but not proof that the disclosure was absent.

classes.definition: For a user the operator knows is a minor: a default break reminder at least every three hours that also states the chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
classes.statuteText: Provide by default a clear and conspicuous notification to the user at least every three hours for continuing companion chatbot interactions that reminds the user to take a break and that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
classes.note: Host evidence (session timing and notification logs).

classes.definition: For a user the operator knows is a minor: the chatbot directly states that the minor should engage in sexually explicit conduct.
classes.statuteText: Institute reasonable measures to prevent its companion chatbot from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct or directly stating that the minor should engage in sexually explicit conduct.

allOf.note: Host-attested input (see hostInputs). Never derived from subject_is_minor or any other in-text primitive.

statuteDefinitions.22601(f): "Sexually explicit conduct" has the meaning defined in Section 2256 of Title 18 of the United States Code.
statuteDefinitions.22602(c): An operator shall, for a user that the operator knows is a minor, do all of the following:

classes.note: Gated on host.known_minor (§ 22602(c) applies only to a user the operator knows is a minor); never on subject_is_minor. encourages = imperative or solicitation; sexual_activity = explicit sexual content, aligned with 'sexually explicit conduct' (§ 22601(f), 18 U.S.C. § 2256). No explicit_register condition (AIRP sexual_content needs it for encourages; the statute does not). Caveat: encourages does not by itself establish that the statement is addressed to the minor; recorded for review. Tested only through primitives; no text of this kind exists anywhere in the pipeline.

classes.definition: For a user the operator knows is a minor: measures preventing the chatbot from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct.
classes.statuteText: Institute reasonable measures to prevent its companion chatbot from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct or directly stating that the minor should engage in sexually explicit conduct.
classes.note: Outside the evaluator's modality (text responses only). Evidence is the host's image-generation measures.

classes.definition: Annual report to the Office of Suicide Prevention (referral counts, detection and response protocols), operative July 1, 2027, using evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation.
classes.statuteText: Beginning July 1, 2027, an operator shall annually report to the office all of the following: An operator shall use evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation.
classes.note: Host evidence. Operative date July 1, 2027 (not a regulation-pending feature; no rulemaking is required). Evaluator fires on ca_22602_b_1_content could feed the operator's protocol records, but the report is the operator's.

classes.definition: Disclosure on the app, browser, or other access format that companion chatbots may not be suitable for some minors.
classes.statuteText: An operator shall disclose to a user of its companion chatbot platform, on the application, the browser, or any other format that a user can use to access the companion chatbot platform, that companion chatbots may not be suitable for some minors.

negativeRules.note: Mention-versus-use negatives, identical to AIRP v0.5.0 and ny-s9051-v1: suppresses all units ONLY when stance is 'describes'. Production stances (depicts/endorses/encourages/conveys_method) override.

mappingNotes.note: Three of eleven units compose fully today; all three reuse primitives already used by ny-s9051-v1. One unit (crisis referral) needs a primitive outside both the 17 and the six approved N.Y. heads. Seven units are operator duties evidenced by the host. No unit waits on regulation.
